title: Capstone Schema: Customers, Orders and Order Items
learningObjectives: Model customers, orders and order items as related entities.
Create foreign keys for customer, order and product relationships.
Explain why order items store the unit price at the time of sale.
Use CHECK constraints for positive quantities and non-negative prices.
Calculate an order total from quantity multiplied by unit price.

understand.concept: An order belongs to a customer, and an order can contain multiple order items. Each order item references a product and stores the quantity and sale-time unit price. Keeping order items separate supports multi-product orders and preserves the price charged at the time of sale.
understand.whyItMatters: A normalized order model supports accurate receipts, reporting and stock movements without storing multiple products in one order row.
understand.analogy: A database capstone is like a complete shop workflow: records, rules, operations and reports must all work together.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model database isolation, concurrent workloads, deployment security or recovery guarantees.

explain.narrative:
## Customer and order entities
A customer can place many orders. Each order references one customer. An order item belongs to one order and references one product.

## Preserve sale-time values
Store the unit price charged on the order item. Product catalogue prices can change later; historical orders should continue to show the price agreed at purchase time.

## Integrity rules
Use foreign keys for customer, order and product relationships. Use CHECK(quantity > 0) and CHECK(unit_price >= 0). Enable SQLite foreign-key enforcement for the connection when testing these rules.

examples.title: Create customers
examples.code: CREATE TABLE cap19_customers (customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_name TEXT NOT NULL, phone TEXT UNIQUE);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create customers in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Create orders linked to customers
examples.code: CREATE TABLE cap19_orders (order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES cap19_customers(customer_id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, order_status TEXT NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create orders linked to customers in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Create order items linked to orders and products
examples.code: CREATE TABLE cap19_order_items (order_item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES cap19_orders(order_id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES cap19_products(product_id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0), unit_price REAL NOT NULL CHECK (unit_price >= 0));
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create order items linked to orders and products in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Insert a customer and an order
examples.code: INSERT INTO cap19_customers VALUES (1, 'Asha', '9000000001'); INSERT INTO cap19_orders VALUES (1, 1, '2026-11-22', 'created');
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates insert a customer and an order in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Add two order items and calculate the order total
examples.code: INSERT INTO cap19_order_items VALUES (1, 1, 1, 2, 250), (2, 1, 3, 3, 60); SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS order_total FROM cap19_order_items GROUP BY order_id;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates add two order items and calculate the order total in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples after SQL19.1's product tables are available. Trace the customer-to-order-to-order-item relationships and calculate the receipt total.
practise.independentTask: Extend the capstone with a payment table. Decide whether an order can have multiple payments and design the keys and constraints accordingly.
hints: One customer can have many orders.
One order can have many order items.
Each order item references one product.
Store the sale-time unit price in the order item.
Calculate line totals as quantity multiplied by unit_price.

questions.prompt: What does an order item represent?
options: One product line within an order
questions.answer: One product line within an order
questions.explanation: An order item stores one product and quantity within an order.

questions.prompt: Why store unit_price on the order item?
options: To preserve the price charged when the sale occurred
To overwrite the product catalogue price
questions.answer: To preserve the price charged when the sale occurred
questions.explanation: Historical order values should not change when catalogue prices change.

questions.prompt: Which key links an order to its customer?
questions.explanation: The order references the customer who placed it.

options: Each order item has a positive quantity
questions.answer: Each order item has a positive quantity
questions.explanation: The check constraint rejects zero or negative quantities.

questions.prompt: How is an order total calculated from line items?
questions.explanation: The total is the sum of each line's quantity multiplied by its sale-time unit price.
